title: Filignano and Selvone, 12 January 1944: the raid at 1500

paras.text: Two batteries of the 2nd Battalion, 67th Coast Artillery (AA), 2.5 km apart in the hills north of Venafro, fired on the same German raid at 1500 on 12 January 1944, the day the French Expeditionary Corps opened its attack toward Sant'Elia and Atina on the Fifth Army's right. Battery F at Selvone logged "12 ME-109 bombing mission, 2 planes destroyed"; Battery G at Filignano, "12 FW 190's, dive bombing ... Two destroyed". Beside them, the German XIV Panzer Corps' reports of the same day.

Context, not identification: the German army reports don't report the Luftwaffe's sorties or losses, and the Luftwaffe's own loss returns have not been seen. The batteries' stations and engagements are also in `../../army/stations.csv` and `../../army/actions.csv` (units `67ca-f`, `67ca-g`).

At 1500 on 12 January Battery F at Selvone logged "12 ME-109 bombing mission, 2 planes destroyed" [[cite:rg64-461580516/p0215]] and Battery G at Filignano "12 FW 190's, dive bombing ... Two destroyed", one exploding in mid-air, the other losing a wing [[cite:rg64-461580516/p0276]]: two batteries 2.5 km apart at the same minute, so one raid and one claim of two, seen from two places and named as two types (inferred). The German XIV Panzer Corps' reports of the day record their own Flak's successes and the enemy's fighter-bomber attacks, and no German aircraft lost [[cite:t314-0543/f0699]]; the Luftwaffe's own loss returns have not been seen.
The folder's files, for anyone reading the records themselves:
`events.yml`: the batteries' engagements and the German reports of the day, in the records' words.

`positions.csv`: the two batteries' stations (placed at the villages; the gun positions aren't given). The German reports' places are points of the January 1944 Bezugspunktkarte, decoded with `tools/bezugspunkt.py` (`basis` `derived`; `guides/BEZUGSPUNKTE.md`): the French attack's front from M 46 to C 11, the points lost at noon, Acquafondata occupied, and the Allied fighter-bombers' target M 28 (Vallerotonda).
`claims.yml`: whether the batteries' claims are matched by a German loss (none found so far), and which unit flew.

t314-0543/f0699.title: Records of German Field Commands, Corps (NARA microfilm publication T-314)

events.words: The French Expeditionary Corps (2nd Moroccan and 3rd Algerian Divisions) attacked on 12 January toward Atina and Sant'Elia, on the Fifth Army's right. Context: that the German report of 06.45 describes this attack is inferred from the date and the sector.
events.source: Blumenson, Salerno to Cassino (U.S. Army in World War II), p. 313

events.original: Beiderseitige Fliegertätigkeit, besonders rege am Nachmittag ... Über dem mittl. Korpsabschnitt vereinzelte Luftkämpfe. Am Nachmittag wurde ein Feindbomber durch Flak abgeschossen. ... Eig. Verschuss 4800
events.translation: Air activity on both sides, especially lively in the afternoon ... isolated air combats over the corps' central sector. In the afternoon an enemy bomber was shot down by Flak. ... Own expenditure 4,800 rounds.
events.note: Two passages of the one report, abridged with "...". Weather: heavy ground mist, clearing at midday, hazy, generally good visibility. No German air attack or German aircraft loss is reported.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: Arko 414, Tagesmeldung vom 12.1.1944

events.original: 6.45 Uhr Abschnitt nördlich M 46 bis C 11 Feindangriff in mindestens Div.-Stärke auf breiter Front nach stärkster langanhaltender Art.-Vorbereitung (auch auf Versorgungswege und Hintergelände)
events.translation: 06.45, in the sector from north of M 46 to C 11: enemy attack in at least division strength on a broad front, after the heaviest and longest artillery preparation (also on supply routes and rear areas).
events.note: Decoded on the January 1944 Bezugspunktkarte: M 46 is 4.6 km west of Battery F at Selvone; C 11 is in the Mainarde (positions.csv).
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: 5. Geb.Div., Tagesmeldung vom 12.1.1944

events.words: "At 1225A fired at 2 ME 109's, 12rds 40mm & 80rds 50 cal expended. No hits claimed, withheld fire as 4 Spitfires appeared in range."
events.source: Battery G, 67th CA (AA), morning report (record of events), 12 Jan 1944

events.original: Rege beiderseitige Fliegertätigkeit, Jabo-Angriffe auf D 14, M 06, D 12, M 28, Strasse C 02 - H 11. Vereinzelte Luftkämpfe. Durch schwere Flak wurde um 14.30 Uhr fdl. ein Flugzeug abgeschossen.
events.translation: Lively air activity on both sides; [enemy] fighter-bomber attacks on D 14, M 06, D 12, M 28, the road C 02 - H 11. Isolated air combats. Heavy Flak shot down an enemy aircraft at 14.30.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: Arko 414, Zwischenmeldung vom 12.1.1944

events.words: "At 1435A fired at 2 ME 109's, 91rds-40mm & 425 rds 50 cal expended. One destroyed."
"2 ME-109 mission unknown flying north over area, no hits. Time 1450A."
events.source: Battery F, 67th CA (AA), morning report (record of events), 12 Jan 1944

events.words: "12 ME-109 bombing mission, 2 planes destroyed, 1500A. Heavy shelling all day."
"At 1500A fired at 12 FW 190's, dive bombing, 206 rds 40mm & 1035 - 50 cal expended. Two destroyed. One plane exploded and disintegrated in mid-air, the other lost wing and fell to earth."

events.original: Nella parte occidentale del fronte dell'Italia meridionale il nemico ha esteso i suoi attacchi anche al settore situato a nord di Venafro. Attacchi lanciati contro le nostre posizioni montane, dopo una forte preparazione di artiglieria, sono stati respinti con elevate perdite per il nemico, mentre due infiltrazioni locali sono state arginate.
events.translation: In the western part of the southern Italian front the enemy also extended his attacks to the sector north of Venafro. Attacks launched against our mountain positions after a heavy artillery preparation were repulsed with heavy losses for the enemy, while two local penetrations were sealed off.
events.note: The communiqué of Berlin, 13 Jan, for 12 Jan, as La Stampa printed it in Italian; it says nothing of German air attacks in Italy that day. The other side's claim.
events.source: La Stampa, 14 Jan 1944, p. 1 (the German communiqué, Berlin, 13 Jan)

claims.question: Did the batteries destroy German aircraft at 1500 on 12 January?
claims.answer: Battery F claimed "2 planes destroyed" of "12 ME-109" at 1500A

claims.question: Did the batteries destroy German aircraft at 1500 on 12 January?
claims.answer: Battery G claimed "Two destroyed" of "12 FW 190's, dive bombing" at 1500A, one exploding in mid-air, one losing a wing
claims.note: The same raid as Battery F's (same time, batteries 2.5 km apart; inferred), so one claim of two, seen from two places; the two name different types.

claims.question: Did the batteries destroy German aircraft at 1500 on 12 January?
claims.answer: No German record read reports a German aircraft lost that day
claims.source: XIV Panzer Corps' reports of 12.1.1944 (army records: they report the enemy's air attacks and their own Flak's successes, not the Luftwaffe's losses)
claims.note: Silence in an army corps' reports is weak evidence: the Luftwaffe's losses were reported in its own channels.

claims.question: Did the batteries destroy German aircraft at 1500 on 12 January?
claims.answer: Two loss lists for II./SG 4 (the Fw 190 fighter-bomber Gruppe then flying over this front) have no loss on 12 January; one aircraft "destroyed without enemy action on an operational flight" on the 11th and another on the 13th
claims.source: Forum posts by L. Rizzotti and B. Lander, 12 O'Clock High, thread 18830 (2009), compiled from the Luftwaffe's loss returns (secondary; the two may share a source, so they count once)
claims.note: Not the loss returns themselves (BA-MA RL 2 III), which are not seen. A damaged aircraft that got home would not be a loss. The Kracker Luftwaffe Archive, also built from the returns, put up a bot check.

claims.question: Which German unit made the 1500 raid?
claims.answer: II./SG 4 flew Fw 190 fighter-bombers over this front and lost aircraft to anti-aircraft fire here before: "10/11/43 Lt. ... KIA Fw.190G-3 (160052) Venafro A/A Fire"; "03/01/44 ... Fw190G-3 (160020) S.Elia A/A"
claims.source: B. Lander's list of II./SG 4 casualties, 12 O'Clock High thread 18830 (secondary)
claims.note: For: Battery G saw dive-bombing Fw 190s. Against: no German record places II./SG 4 over Filignano on 12 January. Battery F saw Me 109s, which would fit an escort or a Bf 109 Jabo unit.

positions.label: Battery G, 67th CA (AA), Filignano
positions.note: The battery's station, 6-19 Jan 1944, giving AA protection to the 938th FA; placed at the village (army/places.csv).

positions.label: Venafro
positions.note: The town; Battery F's station to 5 Jan 1944.

positions.label: Pozzilli
positions.note: The 2nd Battalion's headquarters battery, 8-19 Jan 1944 (army/stations.csv, 67ca-hq2), and Battery F's rear CP.

positions.label: Capriati a Volturno
positions.note: Battery G's station to 5 Jan 1944; the regiment's medical detachment with the 2nd Battalion reported Capriati until 19 Jan.

positions.label: M 46 (the attack's southern end)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, January 1944 edition, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py (jan1944.csv)
positions.note: "6.45 Uhr Abschnitt nördlich M 46 bis C 11 Feindangriff in mindestens Div.-Stärke": the attack front ran from north of M 46 to C 11. Named in t314-0543/f0697.

positions.label: C 11 (the attack's northern end)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, January 1944 edition, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py (jan1944.csv)
positions.note: The other end of the attack front ("nördlich M 46 bis C 11"). Block C fits worse (good to about 1.3 km). Named in t314-0543/f0697.

positions.label: M 20 (lost about noon)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, January 1944 edition, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py (jan1944.csv)
positions.note: "M 20 und C 04 gegen 12 Uhr nach harten wechselvollen Kämpfen in Feindeshand" (M 20 and C 04 in enemy hands about noon after hard, swaying fighting). Named in t314-0543/f0697.

positions.label: C 04 (lost about noon)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, January 1944 edition, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py (jan1944.csv)
positions.note: Lost with M 20 about noon; a counter-thrust "drang bis C 04 vor" and was pushed back. Block C good to about 1.3 km. Named in t314-0543/f0697.

positions.label: M 56 (Acquafondata, occupied)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, January 1944 edition, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py (jan1944.csv)
positions.note: "Vor neuer Widerstandslinie des G.J.R.100 hat nachdrängender Feind M 41, Höhe 1 km nordwestlich M 41, Höhen südwestlich und westlich M 56 besetzt" (in front of the new line of resistance of Gebirgsjäger-Regiment 100, the enemy, following up, occupied M 41, the height 1 km north-west of M 41, and the heights south-west and west of M 56). M 56 is Acquafondata, where Battery F moved on 20 Jan. Named in t314-0543/f0697.

positions.label: M 28 (Vallerotonda, Allied fighter-bomber target)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, January 1944 edition, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py (jan1944.csv)
positions.note: "Jabo-Angriffe auf ... M 28" (the Allies' fighter-bomber attacks on M 28). Named in t314-0543/f0690.
